description: Every finding's cwe_id must be normalised to CWE-NNN format via a field_validator (auto-repair, not a rigid Field(pattern=...) that would reject malformed LLM output — see architecture overview 'auto-repair, not reject')
fix: Add a @field_validator("cwe_id", mode="before") that normalises any input to CWE-NNN format, per normalise_cwe_id() in findings.py

description: output_parser.py's parse_* functions must return a Pydantic model (or None), never a bare str/dict. Agents themselves deliberately use output_type=str (ADR-004/ADR-006) — that is correct, not a violation; the parser is the actual structured-output boundary.
check: python3 -c "import ast; tree = ast.parse(open('src/security_review/output_parser.py').read()); import re; bad = [n.name for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name.startswith('parse_') and n.returns and re.fullmatch(r'(str|dict)(\\s*\\|\\s*None)?', ast.unparse(n.returns))]; print(bad)"
fix: Change the function's return type (and return value) to a Pydantic model such as TriagedFinding, HolisticReviewResult, or ConfigReviewResult
All generated SARIF must set version: 2.1.0 in the top-level object

description: SARIF artifactLocation.uri must use forward slashes — never backslashes. Scoped to sarif/ and passes/sast.py, where SARIF URIs are actually constructed — a blanket src/security_review/ scope also matches unrelated Windows-path-string handling (e.g. cli/tools.py's --language matching) that has nothing to do with SARIF output.
fix: Use str.replace('\\', '/') or PurePosixPath for SARIF URIs. SARIF spec requires forward slashes.

description: SARIF output must include CWE taxonomy block when findings have CWE tags
fix: Call inject_taxonomy() during merge pass to add taxonomies[] with CWE taxa to SARIF runs

description: CWE tags in SARIF must be normalised to external/cwe/cwe-NNN format
fix: Use normalise_cwe_tags() to convert all CWE references to the external/cwe/cwe-NNN convention

description: All CWE IDs referenced in OpenGrep rules must exist in config/taxonomy/cwe.yaml. The taxonomy stores bare numeric YAML keys (e.g. "22":), not literal "CWE-22" strings, so comparison must extract and compare numeric IDs — a literal 'CWE-' substring search against the taxonomy file always returns zero matches and is not a valid check.
check: python3 -c "import re,glob; tax={m.group(1) for l in open('config/taxonomy/cwe.yaml') for m in [re.match(r'^\"?(\\d+)\"?:', l)] if m}; rules={m.group(1) for f in glob.glob('config/rules/opengrep/**/*.yaml', recursive=True) for m in re.finditer(r'CWE-(\\d+)', open(f).read())}; print(sorted(rules-tax, key=int))"
fix: Add missing CWE entries to config/taxonomy/cwe.yaml before adding rules that reference them

description: Every OpenGrep rule must have a matching test file (.py, .cs, or .dockerfile depending on the rule's target language) with ruleid: and ok: annotations
check: for f in $(find config/rules/opengrep/ -name '*.yaml'); do py="${f%.yaml}.py"; cs="${f%.yaml}.cs"; df="${f%.yaml}.dockerfile"; [ -f "$py" ] || [ -f "$cs" ] || [ -f "$df" ] || echo "MISSING TEST: $f"; done
fix: Create a test file (.py, .cs, or .dockerfile matching the rule's languages:) alongside each rule YAML with # ruleid: and # ok: annotations

description: SARIF URIs must never contain absolute paths — normalize to relative paths at SAST output time to prevent leaking internal directory structure and usernames
fix: Call _normalize_sarif_uris(merged, target) after merge_sarif() in run_sast() to strip target_root prefix from all artifact URIs
